archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate attacker)
archetype.definition: A tall, rhythm-based thrower who wins from the pocket by driving the ball into the 10-to-19-yard window and taking selective shots, with his legs now a minor part of the plan.

report.headline: The accuracy leap is real; the touchdown pace is not.
report.take:
Lawrence has always had the frame, the arm and the durability to be a top-ten passer. What he hasn't had, for most of five seasons, is a clean ball: his bad-throw rate ranked 47th or worse in two of his first three years, and last season his CPOE sat at -1.9. Six games into 2026 the most important line in his dossier is that bad-throw rate, down to 8.2% (4th of 37) from 13.9% a year ago. That gain is what lifts everything else. His CPOE is +5.55, a 7.4-point swing from last season, and his EPA per dropback of 0.275 ranks 8th. He is also getting the ball out faster (2.72 seconds, down from 2.87) without throwing shorter. This doesn't look like a scheme hiding him; it looks like a better quarterback.

The damage happens downfield. Throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.711 EPA per attempt, and they account for nearly all of his passing value. Throws under 10 yards are merely solid at 0.162. The intermediate zone is the engine: 53 attempts at 0.623 EPA with a 64.2% success rate. The deep ball (0.943 EPA, three touchdowns) is spectacular but rests on 20 attempts. Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers are where the value goes, with Meyers at 0.563 EPA per target. Brian Thomas Jr. has been a non-factor at 0.088 on 20 targets, which is either an untapped lever or a sign the offense has moved on from him.

The numbers flatter him in two places. The 14 touchdowns lead the league, and his 7.6% TD rate is far above anything in his career. In the red zone he has nine touchdowns while completing just 51.4%, which is conversion luck as much as skill. Week 1's 19-EPA blowout of Cleveland also does a lot of lifting: over Weeks 2-6 his EPA per dropback is 0.202, still very good but not top-five. The interception habit hasn't vanished either. Four picks rank 28th, three of them came on third down, and the two fumbles he got away with show the ball-security risk is bigger than the zero lost suggests.

The last two weeks deserve a close look. Volume jumped, with 39 and 41 attempts producing 331 and 306 yards. His EPA kept climbing game to game, but his CPOE went negative both times (-3.3 and -5.0), and his late-and-close numbers are poor (0.082 EPA, -7 CPOE). Right tackle-level starter Anton Harrison went on IR in the middle of that stretch. My read: the accuracy gains are mostly real and give him a high floor, but expect a top-10 efficiency passer with roughly 30-touchdown output rather than the 40-touchdown pace.

strengths.title: A genuinely cleaner ball
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate has dropped to 8.2% from 13.9% last season and from worse earlier in his career. That is the root of the +7.4 CPOE swing. A change this large, paired with a quicker release, reads as a mechanical or processing improvement rather than noise. It should mostly hold, even if the last two games showed some slippage.

strengths.title: Owns the intermediate middle
strengths.body: The 10-19 yard window is where he does his best work. He has posted 0.623 EPA per attempt there with a 64.2% success rate, and throws over the middle return 0.675 EPA. This is repeatable: it is a large sample, and it suits his size and arm on throws into tight windows. It doesn't depend on hitting long completions.

strengths.title: Avoiding sacks behind a leaky line
strengths.body: His line ranks 19th in hit rate allowed, yet his 5.2% sack rate is well under the league's 6.8%. His time to throw is down from last season, so he is beating pressure with timing rather than holding the ball. That matters more now that a starting tackle is out.

concerns.title: Touchdown rate built to regress
concerns.body: A 7.6% TD rate far exceeds his career norm. His best touchdown year was 29 over 17 games. The red-zone production also outruns the underlying accuracy: nine touchdowns on 51.4% completions. The efficiency is real, but expect the touchdown column to cool toward two a game or a bit under.

concerns.title: Turnovers still lurk on money downs
concerns.body: He has thrown four interceptions (28th of 45), three of them on third down. Two turnover-worthy fumbles went unpunished. His career shows this is a trait, not a blip: he ranked 58th or worse in interceptions in three of five seasons. The fumble luck is the part most likely to turn.

concerns.title: Accuracy fading as volume rose
concerns.body: Over the last three games his CPOE is 4.2 points below his season mark. He was below expectation in both 39- and 41-attempt outings, and his late-and-close numbers are weak. Some of this is a heavier, more aggressive script. Some may be Harrison's absence. Either way, it's the first crack in the core improvement to monitor.

trend.note: After a dud in Denver, his passing EPA rose each week from 7.6 to 11.4 as attempts climbed toward 40. That steady efficiency masks a slide in completion accuracy over the last two games.

nextGame.headline: Rested, at home, against a Colts defense that can't pressure
nextGame.body:
Indianapolis ranks 24th in defensive EPA and 20th against the pass, and its 29th-ranked hit rate means Lawrence should get clean pockets. Short throws against the Colts are easy (23rd in short EPA), and running backs out of the backfield have feasted (RB1s are +5.3 PPR over their averages, last in the league). Their one real resistance is deep, where they rank 11th, and they have choked off WR2s. Expect less of the vertical shot game and more intermediate work plus Bhayshul Tuten as a receiver. Jacksonville comes off a bye with 14 days of rest.

Availability tilts his way. Edge rusher Arden Key is on IR with a projected return after this game, which thins an already weak rush. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies was ruled out the week before. Sauce Gardner was listed doubtful with a week-to-week calf strain as of Oct. 19. The extra week could get him back, so treat his status as the swing on the outside. On Lawrence's side, Harrison remains on IR, but this is the right rush to face without him. One script risk: the Colts' offense ranks 2nd in rushing EPA but 28th passing. A game where Jacksonville builds a lead and leans on the run could trim his attempts back toward 30.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pockets against a quiet rush
keyMatchups.body: The Colts generate hits at the 29th-best rate, and Key is out. His bad-throw and CPOE gains are most bankable when he isn't harried. This is the cleanest setup he has had since the Harrison injury.

keyMatchups.title: Tuten and the short game
keyMatchups.body: Indianapolis has been soft underneath and against backs as receivers. Tuten already returns 0.685 EPA per target. Expect this to be a high-percentage way to move the chains.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots meet a sturdier back end
keyMatchups.body: His deep ball has been his flashiest number on a small sample, and this is one area the Colts handle well. Whether Gardner plays decides how much of that game is available.

nextGame.watch: Whether his completion accuracy rebounds above expectation in a clean pocket, or the two-game CPOE dip carries over even without pressure.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sturdier than in any year since 2022: a cleaner ball, a quicker trigger, and an offense that ranks 4th in passing EPA. That supports top-ten efficiency and roughly 240-280 passing yards a week, especially if the recent mid-to-high-30s attempt counts stick. What won't hold is the touchdown pace. The 40-touchdown projection depends on a red-zone conversion rate his accuracy there doesn't support and a deep-ball EPA built on 20 throws. I'd expect 1.7-2.2 touchdowns a game and an interception most weeks given his history. His rushing has dried up to about half of last year's output, and nothing in the dossier says that returns soon, so his fantasy ceiling rests on his arm.

The swing items are protection and the receiver mix. Harrison's projected return is around Nov. 22, and the IR note allows for a much longer absence. If pressure climbs while he's out, the accuracy gains are what get tested. Getting Brian Thomas Jr. back into the efficient part of the target tree would raise the ceiling.
swingFactors: Anton Harrison's return timeline and pass protection
Whether the CPOE dip of the last two games persists
Brian Thomas Jr.'s re-emergence in the target tree

confidence.note: Six games, with a career-best accuracy jump that looks real but a TD rate and deep-ball sample too small to trust.
